TranslationContext: Approved translations for SOVL rules terminology. Every term in this file carries rules meaning and must be rendered the same way everywhere it appears, in every other file. Fill in the Translation field with the term you want used from now on; the linter then checks the rest of the translation files against it. Definition, Notes and ExampleUsage are reference material for the translator and are not imported into the game.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Skill. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: A unit's training and general fighting ability. Determines hit chance in combat and for Ranged Attacks.
Translations.Notes: Stat block name. Pick one word and never vary it. Do not translate as a generic 'ability' word that collides with [meta.ability].

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Power. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: A unit's physical strength and hitting power. Compared against the defender's Defense to set the Damage Save.
Translations.Notes: Stat block name. Must be distinct from [stat.defense] and from any word used for magical power.
ExampleUsage: Hex of Ruin also reduces Power.
Upgrades Primal Fury to give +2 Power.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Defense. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: A unit's toughness and armour combined. Compared against the attacker's Power to set the Damage Save.
Translations.Notes: Stat block name. English source spells this 'Defense'; treat 'Defence' as the same term.
ExampleUsage: Reanimate also gives +1 Power and Defense.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Attacks. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: How many Attack Rolls each model makes in combat.
Translations.Notes: Stat block name. '+1 Attack' and '+1 Attacks' both refer to this stat and must use the same target noun.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Wounds. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: How many points of damage each model can take before it is removed.
Translations.Notes: Stat block name. The same word is also the unit of damage caused ('one point for each wound caused'); keep them the same word.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Discipline. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: A unit's bravery and willingness to hold. Used for Discipline Tests after combat and heavy casualties.
Translations.Notes: Stat block name.

Translations.Comment: Matches the rendering already dominant in this language's translated strings.
Translations.Definition: How far a unit may move in one activation. Also the maximum range of its charges.
Translations.Notes: The English source is inconsistent here ('Move Speed', 'Movement', 'Movement Allowance'). Use ONE target term for all three.
ExampleUsage: Unit gains +1 Move Speed and ignores Difficult Terrain

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Attack Roll. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: The roll made by an attacking unit to score hits, comparing attacker and defender Skill.
Translations.Notes: Named roll. Keep the same head noun as [roll.damageSave] and [roll.disciplineTest] so the three read as a set.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Damage Save. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: The roll made by the defender against each successful attack, comparing attacker Power to defender Defense. A failed save causes one wound.
Translations.Notes: Named roll. Very common inside ability text; drift here is expensive.
ExampleUsage:
Once per battle: Gain +1 Attack
+1 Damage Save vs Ranged

Translations.Comment: Дисциплина + Проверка, matching the approved Break Test = Проверка боевого духа.
Translations.Definition: A 2d6 roll against the unit's Discipline stat plus Rank Bonus.
Translations.Notes: Named roll. Must use the same word for 'Discipline' as [stat.discipline].

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Break Test. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: The Discipline Test taken by the losing side of an engagement after Combat Score is compared.
Translations.Notes: Named roll. A Break Test is a kind of Discipline Test, so the two terms should look related in the target language.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Ranged Attack. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: An attack made with a missile weapon at a target in range and Line of Sight.
Translations.Notes: Opposed to close combat. Must be distinct from [roll.spellAttack].

Translations.Comment: Contains Заклинание. Distinct from Дальнобойная атака.
Translations.Definition: An attack made by a spell rather than a weapon.
Translations.Notes: Must be distinct from [roll.rangedAttack]; several abilities modify only one of the two.

Translations.Comment: Matches the rendering already dominant in this language's translated strings.
Translations.Definition: Roll the dice again and use the new result.
Translations.Notes: The English source uses 'Reroll' and 're-roll' interchangeably. Use ONE target verb for both, and keep it distinct from the plain verb 'roll'.
ExampleUsage: Unholy Vigour also lets the unit reroll missed Attack Rolls.
Removes the Re-roll penalties from Frost Ward

Translations.Comment: Matches the rendering already dominant in this language's translated strings.
Translations.Definition: A successful Attack Roll. Each hit is followed by a Damage Save.
Translations.Notes: A hit is not yet a wound. Keep the two words distinct.

Translations.Comment: From the corpus. Contains Попадание.
Translations.Definition: Hits scored without rolling an Attack Roll.
Translations.Notes: Must contain the same word used for [roll.hit].

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Turn. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: One full pass through the Charge, Strategic and Combat Phases. A game lasts up to 8 turns.
Translations.Notes: The English source uses 'Turn' and 'Round' for the same thing. Use ONE target word. Do not use a word that also means a single player's activation.
ExampleUsage: Unit gains Regeneration. (restores lost wounds at end of turn)
Once per battle: Gain Flying for one turn.

Translations.Comment: Matches the rendering already dominant in this language's translated strings.
Translations.Definition: One of the three parts of a turn.

Translations.Comment: From the corpus. Натиск + Фаза.
Translations.Definition: First phase of the turn. Charges are declared and resolved.
Translations.Notes: Must combine the target terms for [combat.charge] and [phase.phase].

Translations.Comment: From the corpus.
Translations.Definition: Second phase of the turn. Units manoeuvre, make Ranged Attacks and use abilities.
Translations.Notes: Must combine with the target term for [phase.phase].

Translations.Comment: From the corpus.
Translations.Definition: Third phase of the turn. Engagements are resolved.
Translations.Notes: Must combine with the target term for [phase.phase].

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Activate. Also appears inflected as 'активируется', which is fine.
Translations.Definition: To select a unit and perform its actions for the turn. Also used for one-shot abilities ('Activate once per battle').
Translations.Notes: Use one verb stem for both senses. Keep it distinct from the word used for 'use' or 'cast'.
ExampleUsage: Activate once per battle, +1 Attack and Fearless.
Aura of Vengeance can be activated to affect all Knights

Translations.Comment: CORRECTION. Charge was being translated as 'атака', the same word as the Attack stat, which produced strings like 'Бонус атаки: +1 атака' for what is a charge bonus giving an extra attack. 'Натиск' separates the two cleanly. The existing 'атака' charge strings need rewording.
Translations.Definition: To move a unit into base contact with an enemy in order to fight it.
Translations.Notes: Both noun and verb. Use one stem.
ExampleUsage: Gives 1 extra charge to Arcane Web.
Gives 1 extra charge to Radiant Shield.

Translations.Comment: CORRECTION, see [combat.charge]. Replaces 'Бонус атаки', which collided with the Attack stat.
Translations.Definition: A bonus that applies only in the first turn of combat after the unit charged.
Translations.Notes: Must contain the target term for [combat.charge]. Seen drifting between two different compounds in German; pick one.
ExampleUsage: (Your Knights are Fearless and have Charge Bonus: +1 Attack)

Translations.Comment: Contains Натиск.
Translations.Definition: A charge declared by a unit that already has a charge incoming to its front.
Translations.Notes: Must contain the target term for [combat.charge].

Translations.Comment: Contains Натиск.
Translations.Definition: A higher-priority charge that cancels a charge already declared against the same target.
Translations.Notes: Must contain the target term for [combat.charge].

Translations.Comment: Distinct from Сражение (Battle) and Бой.
Translations.Definition: A grouping of two or more units in base contact, resolved as a unit in the Combat Phase.
Translations.Notes: Rules noun, not a general word for 'battle'. Keep it distinct from [meta.battle].
ExampleUsage: Commander is hidden from your opponent until engaged in combat or damaged.

Translations.Comment: Matches the rendering already dominant in this language's translated strings.
Translations.Definition: The total of wounds caused plus Flank and Rear bonuses. The higher score wins the engagement.
Translations.Notes: Keep the word for 'score' distinct from [meta.points], which means army points cost.
ExampleUsage: Flank and Rear charges add +1 to Combat Score!

Translations.Comment: From the corpus. Contains Атаки.
Translations.Definition: Attacks made by models in the second rank of a unit engaged to its front. One roll per supporting model.
Translations.Notes: Must contain the target term for [stat.attacks].
ExampleUsage: +1 Defense. Extra Rank supporting attacks when not charging.
Unit gets supporting attacks from one extra rank.

Translations.Comment: The physical row of models, as the corpus uses it. Not 'ранг', which is a grade.
Translations.Definition: A row of models across the width of a unit.
Translations.Notes: A physical row of models. Must NOT be translated as a military grade or a leaderboard position. Seen drifting to 'rango' (grade) in Spanish; the correct sense is a row/file.
ExampleUsage: Unit can fire ranged weapons in one additional rank
Unit fights in one additional rank when not charging.

Translations.Comment: From the corpus. Contains Ряд.
Translations.Definition: +1 to Discipline for each rank containing at least 3 models, including the first rank.
Translations.Notes: Must contain the target term for [combat.rank].
ExampleUsage: Units always add their rank bonus to Discipline Tests

Translations.Comment: Matches the rendering already dominant in this language's translated strings.
Translations.Definition: The left or right side of a unit. Charging a flank gives a Combat Score bonus.
Translations.Notes: Geometric side of a unit's base. Part of the set Front / Flank / Rear.
ExampleUsage: Reroll missed Attack Rolls when attacking from Flank or Rear

Translations.Comment: Matches the rendering already dominant in this language's translated strings.
Translations.Definition: The back of a unit. Models engaged in the rear cannot attack.
Translations.Notes: Part of the set Front / Flank / Rear.
ExampleUsage: Reroll missed Attack Rolls when attacking from Flank or Rear

Translations.Comment: Completes the facing set Фронт / Фланг / Тыл.
Translations.Definition: The facing edge of a unit. Line of Sight is a 45 degree arc from the front.
Translations.Notes: Part of the set Front / Flank / Rear.

Translations.Comment: 'Подставка' is the miniature's base.
Translations.Definition: Two units touching base to base, which is what puts them in an Engagement.
Translations.Notes: 'Base' here is the miniature's base, not a fortification.

Translations.Comment: One of the two movement actions, paired with Поворот.
Translations.Definition: Move a unit straight forward. Movement cost equals distance moved.
Translations.Notes: One of the two movement actions, with [movement.pivot].

Translations.Comment: One of the two movement actions, paired with Продвижение.
Translations.Definition: Rotate a unit up to 45 degrees around its centre. Cost depends on unit type.
Translations.Notes: One of the two movement actions, with [movement.advance].

Translations.Comment: Built on 'бегство'. No collision with Полёт (Flying) in Russian.
Translations.Definition: A chaotic move made by a fleeing unit: one d6 per 4 points of movement allowance, in a straight line.
Translations.Notes: Nothing to do with the Flying property. Must NOT share a stem with [property.flying] or players will read it as flight through the air.

Translations.Comment: Opposite of Сплотиться.
Translations.Definition: To break and run. A fleeing unit cannot act except to Rally, and counts as destroyed if it leaves the table.
Translations.Notes: Use one verb stem. Must be distinct from [movement.rally].
ExampleUsage: Fled off the battlefield with zero casualties.

Translations.Comment: Opposite of Бежать.
Translations.Definition: A Discipline Test taken by a fleeing unit to stop fleeing.
Translations.Notes: The opposite of [movement.flee].

Translations.Comment: Abbreviate as ЛВ where the UI is tight, consistently.
Translations.Definition: A 45 degree arc from the front of a unit. Needed to charge, shoot, and cast some spells.
Translations.Notes: The abbreviation 'LoS' appears in UI strings where space is tight. Give it a target abbreviation and use that abbreviation consistently.

Translations.Comment: Matches the rendering already dominant in this language's translated strings.
Translations.Definition: Terrain such as forest or swamp that costs extra movement to enter or start in.
Translations.Notes: Must contain the target term for [movement.terrain].
ExampleUsage: Unit ignores penalties for difficult terrain.
Unit gains +1 Move Speed and ignores Difficult Terrain

Translations.Comment: From the corpus.
Translations.Definition: Terrain that blocks movement completely.
Translations.Notes: Contrasts with [movement.difficultTerrain].

Translations.Comment: Matches the rendering already dominant in this language's translated strings.
Translations.Definition: Features placed on the table that affect movement and Line of Sight.
ExampleUsage: Unit ignores penalties for difficult terrain.
Unit gains +1 Move Speed and ignores Difficult Terrain

Translations.Comment: Contains Дальность.
Translations.Definition: Beyond half a weapon's maximum range. Ranged Attacks at Long Range take -1 to hit.
Translations.Notes: Must contain the target term for [movement.range].

Translations.Comment: Matches the rendering already dominant in this language's translated strings.
Translations.Definition: The maximum distance a Ranged Attack can reach, in inches.
Translations.Notes: Appears constantly in weapon text as 'Range: 24.'. Keep it short; this string sits in a narrow UI column.
ExampleUsage: Upgrades Shadow Bolt to Power 5 and Range 24.

Translations.Definition: The strip of table a player must place their units within during deployment.

Translations.Comment: Shares the развёртывание stem with Зона развёртывания.
Translations.Definition: Deployment ahead of the normal deployment zone, granted by the Scout property.
Translations.Notes: Must contain the target term for [movement.deploymentZone].

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Unit. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: A group of models that moves and fights as one. The basic actor in the game.
Translations.Notes: The single most common rules word in the game. Must be distinct from [unit.model].

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Models. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: A single miniature. A unit is made of models; wounds remove models.
Translations.Notes: Seen drifting between 'modelos' and 'miniaturas' in Spanish. Pick one and use it everywhere, including 'Max Unit size' and model-count strings.
ExampleUsage: Upgrades Raise Dead to raise an additional D3 models.
Recover an extra model that died after each battle.

Translations.Comment: Matches the rendering already dominant in this language's translated strings.
Translations.Definition: The character leading an army. Can activate an ability separately from the unit it joins.
Translations.Notes: Must be distinct from the generic word for a unit champion or leader.

Translations.Comment: From the corpus.
Translations.Definition: Unit type. Base 20x20 or 25x25, movement 8, pivot cost 1.
Translations.Notes: Unit type name.

Translations.Comment: Matches the rendering already dominant in this language's translated strings.
Translations.Definition: Unit type. Base 25x50, movement 16, pivot cost 2.
Translations.Notes: Unit type name.
ExampleUsage: Reroll Ranged and Combat Attacks against Cavalry and Chariots

Translations.Comment: Contains Пехота.
Translations.Definition: Unit type. Base 40x40, movement 12, pivot cost 1.5.
Translations.Notes: Must contain the target term for [unit.infantry].

Translations.Comment: Contains Чудовище.
Translations.Definition: Unit type. Base 50x50, movement 12, pivot cost 1.5.
Translations.Notes: Must contain the target term for [unit.monster].

Translations.Comment: Matches the rendering already dominant in this language's translated strings.
Translations.Definition: A creature unit. Several abilities reroll specifically against Monsters.
Translations.Notes: This is a targeting category in ability text, not just flavour.
ExampleUsage: Reroll Ranged and Combat Attacks against Monsters.

Translations.Comment: Matches the rendering already dominant in this language's translated strings.
Translations.Definition: Unit type. Base 50x100, movement 16, pivot cost 2.
Translations.Notes: A targeting category in ability text ('against Cavalry and Chariots').

Translations.Definition: Unit type. Base 50x50, movement 0.
Translations.Notes: Unit type name.

Translations.Definition: Unit type. Base 25x50, movement 8, pivot cost 1.
Translations.Notes: Unit type name.

Translations.Comment: Distinct from the approved Chariot = Колесница.
Translations.Definition: Unit type. Base 50x100, movement 12, pivot cost 1.5.
Translations.Notes: Unit type name.

Translations.Comment: From the corpus ('Крысиный Рой').
Translations.Definition: Unit type. Base 40x40, movement 8, pivot cost 1.
Translations.Notes: Unit type name. Also appears in enemy army names, where it is flavour rather than the unit type.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UnitProps:Hand Weapon. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: The basic close combat weapon.
Translations.Notes: Also appears as 'Hand Weapon and Shield' and 'Hand Weapon+Shield'; both must use this term plus [equipment.shield].

Translations.Comment: Matches the rendering already dominant in this language's translated strings.
Translations.Definition: Grants +1 Defense with a Hand Weapon, Spear or Lance.
Translations.Notes: Must be distinct from the Shield spell in [meta.spell] contexts.
ExampleUsage: Gives 1 extra charge to Radiant Shield.

Translations.Comment: Chosen over 'Двуручное оружие' because Two Hand Weapons is a separate weapon set (+1 Attack) and would take the two-handed name. If a better-sounding option is wanted, 'Большое оружие' also avoids the collision - worth a native speaker's judgement.
Translations.Definition: Two-handed weapon. +1 Power, Charge Bonus +1 Power.
Translations.Notes: The English source spells this both 'Greatweapon' and 'Great Weapon'. Use ONE target term. Seen drifting between two different German words.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UnitProps:Halberd. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: Polearm. Damage Saves against it are never better than 4+.

Translations.Comment: The infantry weapon. Lance is qualified to keep the two apart, since Russian uses копьё for both.
Translations.Definition: Polearm. With a Shield: +1 Defense and an extra rank of Supporting Attacks when not charging.

Translations.Comment: Qualified to stay distinct from Spear = Копьё.
Translations.Definition: Cavalry weapon. With a Shield: +1 Defense, Charge Bonus +2 Power.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UnitProps:Two Hand Weapons. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: A weapon in each hand. +1 Attack.
Translations.Notes: Must contain the target term for [equipment.handWeapon]. Not the same as [equipment.greatweapon], which is a single two-handed weapon.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Heavy Armor. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: -1 Movement, +1 Defense.
Translations.Notes: Must contain the target term for [equipment.armor].
ExampleUsage: -1 Movement. Ignore the movement penalty from Heavy Armor
-1 Movement. Ignore the movement penalty from Heavy Armor.

Translations.Comment: From the corpus. Contains Броня, parallel to Тяжёлая броня.
Translations.Definition: Light protection with no movement penalty.
Translations.Notes: Must contain the target term for [equipment.armor].

Translations.Comment: Matches the rendering already dominant in this language's translated strings.
Translations.Definition: Protective equipment. Contributes to the Defense stat.
Translations.Notes: The English source uses both spellings; treat them as one term.
ExampleUsage: -1 Movement. Ignore the movement penalty from Heavy Armor

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UnitProps:Fearless. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: Ignores all penalties to Discipline Tests.
Translations.Notes: Named property. Appears both as its own heading and inside other ability text.
ExampleUsage: Activate once per battle, +1 Attack and Fearless.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UnitProps:Frenzy. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: Must charge the closest valid target. Rerolls misses in combat.
Translations.Notes: Named property.
ExampleUsage: Favoured by War. Unit has Frenzy (re-roll failed Attack Rolls in the first round of combat).
All your units have Frenzy (reroll failed Attack Rolls) this turn. Activate once per battle.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UnitProps:Flying. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: Fly Speed 20. Ignores terrain.
Translations.Notes: Named property. Must NOT share a stem with [movement.flightMove], which is a rout move, not flight.
ExampleUsage: Once per battle: Gain Flying for one turn.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UnitProps:Regeneration. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: Unit recovers all missing wounds at end of turn.
Translations.Notes: Named property.
ExampleUsage: Unit gains Regeneration. (restores lost wounds at end of turn)

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UnitProps:Poisoned Attacks. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: Enemies reroll successful Damage Saves against this unit.
Translations.Notes: Must contain the target term for [stat.attacks].
ExampleUsage: Unit gains Poisoned Attacks (enemies re-roll 6s on Damage Saves)

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UnitProps:Scout. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: Forward Deployment.
Translations.Notes: Named property.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UnitProps:Sturdy. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: -1 Movement. Ignores the movement penalty from Heavy Armor.
Translations.Notes: Named property.

Translations.Comment: Chosen over 'Проворный' (nimble/agile): the property is purely +1 Movement, which is speed, not agility.
Translations.Definition: +1 Movement.
Translations.Notes: Named property.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UnitProps:Reanimated. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: -1 Movement. Never fails Discipline Tests.
Translations.Notes: Named property. Distinct from the Reanimate spell; both exist.
ExampleUsage: Increase the move speed of target Reanimated unit by 3 until its next combat.
Restore D3+1 wounds to a Reanimated unit.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Points. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: The cost of a unit in army building, and the currency of end-of-battle scoring.
Translations.Notes: Full form, used where there is room. The abbreviated form is a separate term, [meta.pts] - keep the two visibly related. Distinct from [combat.combatScore], which is the score of a single melee.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:pts. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: Abbreviation of Points, used in army list rows and unit cards where space is tight.
Translations.Notes: Appears glued to the number ('50pts') and separated ('999 pts'). Keep it short - this sits in a narrow column - and keep it recognisable as the short form of [meta.points]. German uses Pkt, Swedish p.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Battle. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: One complete game. 'Activate once per battle' is a common ability limiter.
Translations.Notes: Keep distinct from [combat.engagement], which is a single melee within a battle.

Translations.Comment: From the corpus.
Translations.Definition: The full collection of units a player brings to a battle.

Translations.Comment: From the corpus.
Translations.Definition: The army list a player builds from, e.g. Dwarf Holds or Greenskin Tribes.
Translations.Notes: Faction NAMES are handled per-faction in their own files; this is the generic word.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Warband. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: Smallest army size bracket.
Translations.Notes: One of five army size brackets: Warband, Border Patrol, Battalion, Legion, Unrestricted. Translate the five as a coherent ladder of increasing size.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Border Patrol. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: Second army size bracket.
Translations.Notes: See [meta.warband].

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Battalion. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: Third army size bracket.
Translations.Notes: See [meta.warband].

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Legion. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: Fourth army size bracket.
Translations.Notes: See [meta.warband]. Also appears in the faction name 'Abyssal Legions', which is separate.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Unrestricted. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: Largest army size bracket, with no list restrictions.
Translations.Notes: See [meta.warband].

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Spell. Also appears inflected as 'Заклинания', which is fine.
Translations.Definition: A magical effect activated by a caster.
Translations.Notes: Keep distinct from [meta.ability] and [meta.enchantment].

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Cantrips. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: A lesser spell, available without spending points.
Translations.Notes: Must be distinguishable from [meta.spell].

Translations.Comment: Distinct from Умение (Skill) and Заклинание (Spell).
Translations.Definition: A non-spell effect a unit or commander can activate.
Translations.Notes: Keep distinct from [stat.skill] and [meta.spell].

Translations.Comment: Matches the approved Чары оружия.
Translations.Definition: A purchasable magic item or weapon upgrade.
Translations.Notes: Keep distinct from [meta.spell] and [meta.banner].

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Weapon Enchantments. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: UI section for enchantments that upgrade a weapon.
Translations.Notes: Must contain the target term for [meta.enchantment], and pair with [meta.itemEnchantment].

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Item Enchantments. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: UI section for enchantments carried as items.
Translations.Notes: Must contain the target term for [meta.enchantment], and pair with [meta.weaponEnchantment].

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Banners. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: A standard carried by a unit, bought like an enchantment.
Translations.Notes: The English source also says 'Standard' for the same thing (e.g. 'Cursed Standard'). Use ONE target word.

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:Level. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: A unit's campaign progression rank. Gained with XP.
Translations.Notes: Campaign progression, not difficulty. Keep distinct from 'Challenge Level'.
ExampleUsage: Newly recruited units gain an additional level
Newly recruited units gain an additonal level

Translations.Comment: Seeded from the existing translation in UI:XP. Confirm this is the term you want.
Translations.Definition: Experience points earned by units in campaign play.
Translations.Notes: Short form used in tight UI. Keep the target form short; leaving it as 'XP' is acceptable in most languages.

Translations.Comment: Names a UI section.
Translations.Definition: A notable achievement a unit earns during a battle, awarding XP.
Translations.Notes: Flavourful but load-bearing: it names a UI section.

Translations.Comment: From the corpus. States as a set: Unclaimed = Не захвачена, Contested = Оспаривается, Claimed = Захвачена.
Translations.Definition: A marker on the battlefield that can be claimed for scoring.
Translations.Notes: Related UI states: Unclaimed, Contested, Claimed. Translate those three as a coherent set.

Translations.Comment: This language's dice notation. Corpus evidence: D notation throughout.
Translations.Definition: A six-sided die.
Translations.Notes: Some languages have their own dice notation - German writes W6 and W3 for D6 and D3. Either keep the English notation or use the local convention, but use the same one in every file. The number is part of the term: D3 is a separate term and must never become D6.

Translations.Comment: Matches this language's D6 notation. A different number of results from D6 - never merge the two.
Translations.Definition: A three-sided result, rolled on a D6 and halved.
Translations.Notes: Some languages have their own dice notation - German writes W3. Match whatever convention this language uses for [meta.d6]. Never write this as D6: it is a different number of results.
ExampleUsage: Upgrades Raise Dead to raise an additional D3 models.
-1 Movement. Never fails Discipline tests, loses D3 wounds on lost combat.

Translations.Comment: Do not translate - leave exactly as written in the English.
Translations.Definition: The name of the game.
Translations.Notes: Never translate or transliterate.
ExampleUsage: The dice in SOVL are mathematically fair. They are also cursed by a demon, who is evil. But they are fair!
